timeline.title: Milestones in Economic System Shifts
timeline.description: Key historical transitions and frameworks defining modern economic classifications.

cards.details: Classical theory formalized market-based capitalism, where private actors drive decisions and the state remains minimalist.
The rise of the USSR established the command (socialist) economy model, replacing the price mechanism with state central planning.
Independent India adopted a Mixed Economy model, giving a key role to public sectors (commanding heights) alongside private business.
India transitioned from a highly regulated, closed mixed economy to an open, globalized mixed economy through Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Hacks
mnemonics.description: Simple associations to remember economic typologies.

items.title: Mnemonic 1: The Three C's of Capitalist vs. Socialist
items.decryption: **Capitalism** focuses on **C**ompetition, **C**onsumer choice, and market pricing. **Socialism** focuses on state **C**ontrol, **C**entralized planning, and public welfare.

items.title: Mnemonic 2: Open vs Closed Economy Balance
items.decryption: A **Closed** economy behaves like a **c**age: $Y = C + I + G$ (no foreign trade $X-M$). An **Open** economy is like the **o**cean: $Y = C + I + G + (X - M)$.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Trap 1: Socialist vs Communist Economies: In a Socialist economy, resources are owned by the state, but people are paid based on their labor output. In a Communist economy, all private property is abolished, and distribution is based on need ('From each according to ability, to each according to need'). UPSC often treats them identically, but they differ structurally.

Trap 2: Closed Economy in Reality: No modern country is a 100% closed economy. Even North Korea engages in limited trade. A closed economy is a theoretical model ($Y = C + I + G$) used to study domestic economic balances without external exchange rates.

Trap 3: World Bank Income Classifications: These classifications are based on **GNI per capita** (Gross National Income) using the Atlas method, NOT GDP per capita. India is currently classified as a **Lower-Middle Income** economy.

Trap 4: Dual Economy: A dual economy refers to the coexistence of a highly advanced, capital-intensive formal sector alongside a low-productivity, labor-intensive informal or traditional sector (common in developing countries like India).

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Comprehensive analysis of capitalist, socialist, mixed, developed, developing, open, and closed economic systems.

sections.title: 1. Classification by Control & Ownership: Market, Command, and Mixed
sections.content:
Economic systems are classified by how decisions are made and who owns productive resources.

Capitalist (Market) Economy
  • Ownership: Private property rights, private enterprise.
  • Coordinating Force: Price mechanism (invisible hand of demand and supply), profit motive, consumer sovereignty. State role is regulatory.
Socialist (Command) Economy
  • Ownership: Public/State ownership of all key resources and factories.
  • Coordinating Force: Central planning commission. Decisions on what, how, and for whom to produce are administrative. Social welfare over profit.

Mixed Economy: Coexistence of public sector and private enterprise. The state controls vital industries ('commanding heights' like defense and infrastructure) while the market manages consumer goods (e.g., India's post-independence model, transitioning towards market-led open mixed setup after 1991).

sections.title: 2. Classification by Development & Global Trade
sections.content:
Economies are categorized globally based on per capita income levels and trade openness.

  • World Bank Income Classifications (GNI Per Capita - Atlas Method):
    • Low-Income: GNI per capita below threshold (typically < $1,135).
    • Lower-Middle Income: India falls in this category (approx. GNI per capita between $1,136 and $4,465).
    • Upper-Middle Income: e.g., China, Brazil (approx. GNI per capita between $4,466 and $13,845).
    • High-Income: Developed economies (GNI per capita > $13,845; e.g., USA, Germany, Japan).
  • Open vs. Closed Economies:
    • Open Economy: Engages in international trade (exports/imports) and financial flows. GDP identity: $Y = C + I + G + (X - M)$. Highly integrated with global capital markets.
    • Closed Economy: No trade or capital flows with foreign nations. GDP identity: $Y = C + I + G$ (Net exports $NX = 0$). Autarky state.

sections.title: 3. Structural Sectors & Formalization
sections.content:
Economic structures undergo transitions as they develop, manifesting dual properties.

  • Structural Transitions: Fisher-Clark thesis states that economies transition from agrarian (primary sector dominance) to industrial (secondary sector dominance) and eventually service-dominated (tertiary dominance) states as they grow.
  • Formal vs. Informal Economies:
    • Formal Economy: Activities that are registered, taxed, and monitored by the government. Workers enjoy social security, minimum wage, and contract protection.
    • Informal (Shadow) Economy: Unregistered and untaxed economic activities. High prevalence in developing economies (e.g., India's informal sector employs over 85% of the total workforce), characterized by low social security and vulnerable employment.
  • Dual Economy: Coexistence of a modern, technology-driven formal sector alongside a low-productivity, labor-intensive traditional/informal sector in the same nation.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following describes the core coordinating mechanism of a capitalist (market) economy?
opts: A central planning committee establishing targets
The price mechanism driven by demand and supply
State directives on minimum wage and distribution
mockTestQuestions.sol: In a capitalist market economy, resource allocation, consumption, and production are coordinated by prices determined freely in the market.

mockTestQuestions.q: Under the World Bank's income-level classification system, India is currently categorized as a:
mockTestQuestions.sol: India belongs to the Lower-Middle Income category, based on GNI per capita thresholds computed via the Atlas method.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which of the following equations represents the macroeconomic identity of a completely closed economy?
mockTestQuestions.sol: A closed economy does not trade internationally, meaning exports (X) and imports (M) are zero, leaving $Y = C + I + G$.

mockTestQuestions.q: The coexistence of a high-tech, capital-intensive formal service sector alongside a labor-intensive, low-productivity informal sector is known in economics as a:
mockTestQuestions.sol: A Dual Economy features the structural coexistence of modern/advanced and traditional/underdeveloped sectors side by side.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which economic policy resolution in India first formalized the Mixed Economy model, reserving key sectors for state monopoly while allowing private enterprises in others?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948 was independent India's first policy document, laying down the mixed economy blueprint.

mockTestQuestions.q: In a socialist economy, economic decisions on 'what to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce' are primarily resolved by:
mockTestQuestions.sol: Socialist or command economies substitute the market price mechanism with centralized administrative decisions based on social welfare.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The World Bank classifies economies using Gross National Income (GNI) per capita rather than GDP per capita.
2. In a communist system, resources are owned by the state but workers are paid strictly based on their output.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because communism distributes goods based on need, whereas socialism distributes based on work/output.

mockTestQuestions.q: An economy that does not permit any foreign direct investment (FDI) or international capital flows but allows merchandise import/export is classified as:
opts: A partially open economy (open to trade but closed to capital flows)
mockTestQuestions.sol: Opening to trade while restricting capital accounts makes an economy partially open, unlike autarky (completely closed to all).

mockTestQuestions.q: The informal sector in developing countries is best characterized by which of the following features?
opts: High degree of regulation and strict tax compliance
Access to formal social security benefits for all workers
Vulnerable, unregistered employment and lack of social safety nets
mockTestQuestions.sol: The informal economy operates outside state registration and taxation, characterized by lack of written contracts and social safety nets.

mockTestQuestions.q: Which thesis explains the chronological shift of labor force and output share from primary to secondary and tertiary sectors as an economy grows?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Fisher-Clark structural thesis details the transition of employment and GDP dominance from primary to industrial and then service activities.
